column1: # POLARIS key registry — every ops/CONVENTIONS.md key the kit reads, as DATA.
# TAB-separated: key<TAB>since<TAB>default<TAB>absent-cost      ('#' lines and blank lines ignored)
#   key          the CONVENTIONS.md header key, spelled exactly as `cfg` reads it
#   since        the kit version that introduced it
#   default      the EFFECTIVE value when the key is ABSENT — what the repo already behaves as, not
#                what INIT happens to write. For the three autonomy knobs these are the 6.0 values
#                (ops/contracts/hands-free-knobs.md v2), NOT the pre-6.0 ones. A `<placeholder>`
#                means there is no effective value: the key is optional, unset does nothing, and the
#                placeholder is what a human types in its place.
#   absent-cost  one plain-English line — what the repo loses, or behaves as, while the key is unset
# Rows DOCUMENT; they never execute. Adding a row is data, not behavior. `polaris doctor` reports
# which of these an installed CONVENTIONS.md lacks, and `polaris adopt` appends one commented stub
# per absent key. Contract: ops/contracts/key-registry.md. ORDER IS MEANINGFUL — doctor names the
# first six absent keys in the order they appear below.

column4: branches cut from and merge into main; a repo whose trunk is named anything else breaks
locks stay on this machine; several machines sharing one repo need claim-branch
merges land as one batch and halve on red; paranoid tests after every single merge
agents talk to you in plain friendly English; technical makes them dense and terse
the Planner offers Builder panes once; wt opens them for you, off only prints kickoffs
a work request runs the whole loop in one chat; panes stops the conductor after planning
polaris route answers in bare tier words — no real model name reaches a spawn or a pane
same for the mid tier — ordinary tasks run on whatever the platform defaults to
same for the cheap tier — small tasks are never routed to a cheaper model
unset composes the hands-free trio since 6.0; autonomy: standard is the one-line opt-out
unset proceeds past a clean plan since 6.0; confirm waits for your go every time
unset lets Builders default reversible spec details since 6.0; ask returns every question
unset lets EVOLVE apply its inert allowlist since 6.0; confirm queues every item for approval
a run stops after the approved plan's own tasks; queue and backlog reach further
caps planner-promotion rounds under drain: backlog — ignored under any other drain mode
a run builds at most 12 tasks, then integrates what landed and reports
a run takes no new work 90 minutes after kickoff — checked at wave boundaries only
a run spawns at most 20 subagents in total
the Check phase retries a red suite at most twice before handing you the failures
the runtime QA scout spawns only when uat: is empty AND the run touched a runnable: path
this repo declares no runnable surface, so qa_scout: auto resolves to off

sweep warns on active locks older than 4 hours

board events and gates reach nothing outside the terminal you happen to be watching
a fresh worktree installs no dependencies, so the first verify: on a real repo fails
a Builder that runs build: is rejected for dirtying tracked build output it does not own
seal merges and pushes the base locally; pr pushes only integrate/<date> and prints a PR URL
a lone small task takes the express lane; off spends the full pipeline on everything
where seal writes the per-sprint report and polaris report regenerates it
nothing proves a task green — the wave gate, qa and CI all have no suite to run
no lint gate runs before a task reaches review
no type gate runs before a task reaches review
no build gate runs before a task reaches review
at most 3 Builder panes open themselves; the printed kickoffs stay uncapped
a second session waits 10 minutes for the integration lane before it gives up
an integration lease held this long counts as crashed and may be stolen
